crop.notes: Whole item, headline to closing rule.

summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican quoted John Sweeney, Ben Hogan's old trainer, recalling the Allen-Hogan fight: he claimed a foul after two rounds, the armed crowd cut into the ring, and the referee called it a draw.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'The Republican: St. Louis, Tuesday Morning, April 3, 1888'; the paper was not yet renamed the St. Louis Republic.

facts.fact: Ben Hogan's fight with Allen was declared a draw by referee Bill Riley after Hogan's corner claimed a foul in the second round and the crowd cut into the ring with knives and revolvers, according to Hogan's trainer John Sweeney

notes: Recollection given in 1888; the article does not give the fight's date or place (the fight itself was in 1873). It also says Hogan put up $1,000 of his own money and that this was Hogan's last fight.
